units.title: Mixed Conditionals
units.intro: Mixed conditionals join a past condition with a present result, or a present condition with a past result.
items: If I had studied harder, I would be a doctor now.
If she had taken the map, she wouldn't be lost now.
If I weren't afraid of heights, I would have climbed the tower.
If + past simple, would have + p.p.
If he were careful, he wouldn't have broken the vase.
If I had slept early, I wouldn't be tired now.
= I didn't sleep early, so I am tired now.
Mixed conditionals talk about things that are not true.

acts.title: Choose the correct form
rows: If I had eaten breakfast, I ... hungry now.
If she ... the bus, she would be here now.
If he spoke English, he ... the job last year.
If we ... the tickets, we would be at the match now.

acts.title: What does it mean?
rows: If I had saved money, I would have a car now.
I didn't save money, and I don't have a car.
I saved money, and I have a car.
If he weren't shy, he would have spoken at the party.
He is shy, and he didn't speak.
He isn't shy, and he spoke.
If they had left earlier, they would be home now.
They didn't leave early, so they aren't home.
They left early and are home.
If I knew her number, I would have called her.
I don't know her number, so I didn't call.
I know her number and I called.

units.title: Inversion
units.intro: After some negative words at the start of a sentence, we put the auxiliary before the subject, like a question. It makes the sentence stronger.
items: Never have I seen such a beautiful sky.
Never had she felt so happy.
Rarely do we see snow in the desert.
Not only did she win, but she also broke the record.
Not only is he clever, but he is also kind.

acts.title: Choose the correct inversion
rows: Not only ... fast, but she also swims well.

acts.title: Which sentence means the same?
rows: I have never tasted such good dates.
Never have I tasted such good dates.
Never I have tasted such good dates.
She sings and she also plays the oud.
Not only does she sing, but she also plays the oud.
Not only she sings, but also plays the oud.

units.title: Cleft Sentences
units.intro: Cleft sentences help us focus on one part of the sentence: It was … that / who …, or What … is ….
items: It was my teacher who encouraged me to read.
It was Ali who found the key.
It was in Madinah that I met my best friend.
It is / was + thing / place / time + that
It was on Friday that we travelled.
What I need is a good dictionary.
What she wanted was a quiet room.

acts.title: Choose the right word
rows: It was Sara ... won the prize.
It was at the airport ... I lost my bag.
It ... my father who taught me to swim.

acts.title: Which cleft sentence is correct?
rows: Focus on 'Ahmed': Ahmed broke the window.
It was Ahmed who broke the window.
It was the window who Ahmed broke.
Focus on 'a rest': I need a rest.
What I need is a rest.
What is a rest I need.
It was yesterday that we arrived.
It was we that arrived yesterday.
Focus on 'the noise': The noise woke me up.
It was the noise that woke me up.
What the noise was woke me up.

units.title: Participle Clauses
units.intro: Participle clauses make sentences shorter. We use -ing for active ideas and the past participle for passive ideas.
items: Hearing the bell, the students ran out.
Feeling tired, I went to bed early.
Built in 1900, the house is very old.
= The house, which was built in 1900, …
Written in Arabic, the book is easy for me.
Having finished my homework, I went out to play.
= After I had finished my homework, …
Having eaten lunch, we continued our trip.

acts.title: Choose the correct participle
rows: ... the news, she started to cry.
... in 2010, the bridge is still strong.
... his keys, he couldn't open the door.
The boy ... near the window is my brother.

acts.title: Which sentence means the same?
rows: Because I felt cold, I closed the window.
Feeling cold, I closed the window.
Felt cold, I closed the window.
The cake, which was made by Mum, was delicious.
Made by Mum, the cake was delicious.
Making by Mum, the cake was delicious.
After he had read the letter, he smiled.
Having read the letter, he smiled.
Have read the letter, he smiled.
When she opened the box, she found a gift.
Opening the box, she found a gift.
Opened the box, she found a gift.

units.title: Future Perfect
units.intro: We use the future perfect for an action that will be finished before a time in the future, and the future perfect continuous for how long an action will have continued.
items: By 2030, they will have built a new airport.
By Friday, I will have finished the book.
By 8 o'clock, the shop will have closed.
by tomorrow / by next year / by then
By the time you arrive, we will have eaten.
Next June, I will have been studying English for ten years.
By noon, we will have been driving for five hours.

acts.title: Choose the correct form
rows: By next week, I ... my exams.
By 10 p.m., she ... for six hours.
By the time we get there, the film ...

acts.title: Complete the sentence
rows: By the end of this year, I ...
Next month, they ... in this house for a year.
By the time you wake up, I ...

units.title: would rather & had better
units.intro: We use would rather for preferences, had better for strong advice, and It's time for things that should happen now.
items: I'd rather walk than take the bus.
She'd rather stay at home tonight.
You'd better take an umbrella. It's going to rain.
It's time to go to bed.

acts.title: Choose the correct form
rows: We'd better ... noise. The baby is sleeping.

units.title: Reading Time
units.intro: Read the texts, then answer the questions.

acts.title: My Grandfather's Farm
acts.html:
My Grandfather's Farm 🌴

It was my grandfather who taught me to love the desert.
Never have I seen a sky as full of stars as the one above his farm.
Having lived there for fifty years, he knows every hill and every tree.
If he hadn't planted those palm trees long ago, the farm wouldn't be so green today.

acts.title: Answer
rows: Who taught the writer to love the desert?
How long has the grandfather lived on the farm?
Why is the farm green today?
He planted palm trees long ago.
“Never have I seen …” is an example of …

acts.title: Huda's Dream
acts.html:
Huda's Dream 🩺

By the end of this year, Huda will have finished school.
Rarely does she miss a lesson, and she would rather read than watch TV.
Encouraged by her teachers, she has decided to study medicine.
“You'd better start preparing now,” her mother told her with a smile.

acts.title: Answer
rows: What will Huda have done by the end of the year?
What has she decided to study?

acts.title: True or False?
rows: The grandfather knows every hill and every tree.
The farm is not green today.
The writer's teacher taught him to love the desert.
